title: Enrollment Rights Under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies: the Open Enrollment Period and Guaranteed Issue
content:
Every applicant has one open enrollment period for a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, during which the plan must issue any policy it sells at the standard rate with no health questions and no waiting period for a condition treated before issue.

### The open enrollment window

The plan receives the signed application no later than the last day of the open enrollment period counted from the date the applicant's Medicare Part B enrolment began. That date is taken from the member's own profile, and the date the application arrived from the policy record; the two are correlated by the member applying, and the condition is settled before the application is recorded. Calendar months are counted from the day of the month the Part B enrolment began, a month that has no matching day ends on its last day, the final day of the period is itself inside it, and calendar days and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar months. The length of the period is the number of calendar months the plan letter carries as its open enrollment period.

*Boundary cases, hypothetical.* Where the period runs 6 calendar months, an application received on the final day of that sixth month is inside the period and one received the day after it is outside. Where the enrolment began on a day of the month the sixth month does not have, that month's last day is the final day of the period, and an application received on that last day is in time.

### Guaranteed issue outside that period

Outside that period a guaranteed issue right still requires the plan to issue certain of its policies without health questions, and the applicant must show the event that gave them the right rather than merely assert it. A guaranteed issue right lasts sixty-three calendar days from the loss of the coverage that gave rise to it, and the plan tells an applicant who is inside that window which of its policies they may have without answering questions.

### Two matters that follow

An applicant who is inside their open enrollment period is never underwritten even where they volunteer health information, and the plan records the issue basis so that the rate and the waiting period can never be applied by mistake.

A policy the plan letter does not offer on a guaranteed issue right may still be applied for with health questions, and the applicant is told which of the two routes they are on before the application is taken.
